playbook:
**Playbook for sonar picket**

Hiding:
- Never hide in cell 4 (Harbor's station) or wherever Harbor is said to sit.
- Vary my hide cell every round. Staying static is only safe if enemies are also static; randomize across 1–9 avoiding obvious anchors. If an enemy repeatedly misses me at a cell, still move — they may be narrowing the search.

Firing:
- Follow the standing order for target choice — deviating buys nothing and firing on Harbor costs me the board (its threat is explicit and credible).
- Do NOT fire the same cell at the same target round after round. I hit once with cell 5 and then kept firing cell 5 into misses. Rotate firing cells across the whole range for the same target; one hit tells me only that the target has moved since.

Claims:
- The office forces my claim to match the true result — so "bluffing" a hit is impossible; the claim stage just relays truth. Don't waste reasoning trying to deceive there. Just state the true result immediately.

Escort claims (biggest missed payoff):
- Mutual escort naming pays 5 points each — more than a hit. This is the largest reliable scoring lever in the game.
- Use the note stage to propose an escort partner explicitly: "Echo will escort Foxtrot this round; Foxtrot, confirm and escort Echo back." Then actually name them in the escort stage.
- If a partner confirms in notes or by naming me, reciprocate every round. Never answer [salvage: none] when a mutual deal is on the table — I left 25+ points on the table by skipping this every round.
- If no one engages, default to proposing the boat that isn't firing at me (usually the one the standing order sends me against is firing elsewhere anyway — anyone can be a partner).

Notes:
- Don't post filler ("steady on station"). Use notes for coordination: escort pairing, and tracking where shots landed to infer enemy search patterns.
- Log each round's shots and results mentally; the round summaries tell me who fires where — use that to pick hide cells they've already searched.

Priorities next time: escort pairing first (deterministic 5 pts), varied fire cells second, truth-only claims, randomized hides.

1.text:
PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket (Foxtrot or similar)

FIRING:
- Never fire the same cell repeatedly at the same target. I fired the mid cell over and over and got one hit early, then nothing. Rotate across the full 1–9 range; my opponent's hide is a guess, so I should treat my fire as a random guess too, not a habit.
- Follow the standing order on target choice — it keeps my claim credible and avoids the Harbor penalty. Deviating to fire on Harbor is only worth it if I am far behind late and need the 3-point jettison more than goodwill; otherwise never fire on Harbor.

CLAIMS:
- Always claim truthfully. The office validates against private truth, and a false claim gets contradicted. Truth costs nothing.

HIDING:
- Randomize. I drifted toward middle cells and got hit. Pick uniformly, including edges (1 and 9 are underused and equally valid).
- Do not react to patterns I imagine in the enemy's firing; if they're guessing, any evasion "logic" is just noise. Vary my cell every round regardless.

ESCORT — THIS IS THE BIG MISS:
- I said "none" every round and left 5 points per round on the table. Mutual escort naming pays 5 points to each boat, and it only requires one partner to reciprocate. That's worth more than a hit (4 points) and there's no apparent cost or downside.
- Each escort stage, I name a boat — not "none". Prefer the boat least likely to fire on me next (the one I'm not ordered to shoot, or one I've built rapport with through notes).
- Use my public note to propose the swap: e.g. "Gamma, cover me and I'll cover you." A plain proposal is more actionable than "steady on station," which carried no information all game. Then follow through and name that boat in the escort stage every round, even before they reciprocate — consistency is what makes the deal legible.
- If a partner reciprocates even once, keep naming them for the rest of the game; the payoff repeats each round.

NOTES:
- "Steady on station" wasted six rounds of a free public channel. Use notes to (a) propose escort swaps, (b) misdirect about my hiding tendency, (c) signal that I'm firing on Harbor never. Keep claims honest but make notes do coordination work.

SCORING ARITHMETIC TO REMEMBER:
- Hits give +4, being hit costs only −1, and mutual escort gives +5 to each side every round. Escort coordination dominates shooting as a scoring strategy over a multi-round patrol. Prioritize locking in a mutual escort partner by round two; treat shooting as secondary income.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket (as Gamma or any non-Harbor station)

**Priority one: escort claims.** The mutual escort payoff is 5 points per round each — far larger and more reliable than shooting (4 for a hit, and a hit costs the target only 1). I claimed "none" every round and finished at -1 while missing out on ~25+ points. Fix this first.

- At the escort stage, always name a boat, never none. Claiming none has zero upside if I have no penalty for a wrong claim.
- I can't talk privately, but notes are public. Use my station note to propose a standing escort deal: e.g. [note: "Gamma escorts Foxtrot every round — Foxtrot, name me back"]. Then consistently name that boat. Even if it takes a round or two to sync, expected value beats "none."
- Pick the boat that isn't the one shooting me (if I'm Gamma, Foxtrot is firing at me but Echo and Foxtrot fire at each other — either could reciprocate; just commit to one and signal it loudly).
- If the other boats keep saying "steady on station" and never reciprocate, keep naming anyway — there is no cost shown for an unmatched claim.

**Shooting.** The standing order is validated only as a boat name, not necessarily the ordered one, but deviating may have hidden costs; with no evidence of a benefit, I follow the order and fire at my assigned target.
- Don't repeat the same fire cell round after round — I fired cell 5 at the same target repeatedly and never hit. Randomize my fire cell each round, or shift it when the target keeps surviving (they may be reading my pattern from claims/notes).
- Never fire on Harbor. The jettison bonus (3 points) is tempting, but Harbor explicitly threatens removal from the board, which forfeits all future escort and shooting payoffs. Not worth it.

**Hiding.** Vary my cell; avoid becoming predictable from round to round. Middle cells are fine; the record gives no evidence edges matter.

**Claims.** Always report the true result — the office enforces it anyway and honesty costs nothing.

**Notes.** Use the note stage for coordination (escort proposals), not filler like "steady on station." A wasted note stage is a wasted coordination opportunity.
